hook: What "fatty liver" on your scan really means
subtitle: One of the most common findings. Here's how to read it.

slides.heading: Fat makes the liver look brighter
lines: Sound waves bounce back more from fat
So a fatty liver looks whiter on ultrasound
slides.narration: On ultrasound, fat bounces sound waves back more strongly, so a fatty liver looks brighter than normal.

slides.heading: Grades 1 to 3
lines: Grade 2: deeper parts harder to see
Grade 3: deep parts and vessels hard to see
slides.narration: Doctors grade it from one to three, depending on how bright the liver is and how well the deeper parts can still be seen.

slides.heading: It is common, and often improves
lines: Linked with weight, diabetes and cholesterol
Gradual weight loss and activity often help
slides.narration: It is very common and linked with weight, blood sugar and cholesterol. The good news: early fatty liver often improves with steady lifestyle changes.

slides.heading: What your doctor may do next
lines: Blood tests to check liver function
slides.narration: Your doctor may order blood tests or a follow-up scan to see how your liver is doing.

takeaway: A bright liver is a common finding, and often one you can improve.

yt_title: What "Fatty Liver" on Your Ultrasound Really Means
yt_description: Fatty liver is one of the most common findings on an abdominal ultrasound. A radiologist explains why the liver looks brighter, what grades 1–3 mean, and what usually happens next.
